method: DOM accessible-name heuristic with associated-label resolution, keyboard focus reachability, reduced-motion media context and forced-colors media context. This is not a substitute for VoiceOver/NVDA/manual WebKit review.

results.observed: Home, Study, Vocabulary, Word Detail, Weak Words and Dictation visible controls had names after resolving aria-label, aria-labelledby, title and associated labels. Settings had one independent hidden file input without a name.
Focus reached the featured-word link and Study exit button; computed focus outline width was 3px in both checks.
On page surfaces the local computed samples included body 13.61:1, page h1 13.61:1, page supporting paragraph 4.84:1, and Word Detail secondary button 6.45:1.
results.limitation: Photographic surfaces require pixel-composited contrast review; do not infer their final ratio from transparent CSS backgrounds.

results.observed: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce Study session had no horizontal overflow and no console/page/request errors; no motion system was changed.
forced-colors: active Settings session had no horizontal overflow; the same hidden file input was the only unnamed control.
No product change in this planning branch; the v1.4.1 Safe Area and WebKit gates remain the release baseline and are not reinterpreted by this DOM-only run.

findings.title: Hidden file input name
findings.recommendedValidation: Run the actual file-picker trigger with a screen reader and choose Path A (hidden input not independently exposed) or Path B (explicit accessible name). Preserve import, backup, restore, file-picker trigger and DB behavior.
